abstract: The days following decompression surgery for acute spinal cord injury (SCI) are a critical period for postoperative monitoring. abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a cornerstone of brain-computer interfaces and clinical neuro-diagnostics due to its non-invasiveness and high temporal resolution. While lightweight architectures like EEGNet offer favorable parameter efficiency, their reliance on fixed convolution kernels and...

title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
abstract: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. This structure...

title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
abstract: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. The corpus comprises a quota-based...

title: Where and Why is Grounded Reasoning Useful?
abstract: Grounded reasoning, where a model outputs text coordinates of relevant locations in chain-of-thought reasoning, is a common strategy for solving complex visual reasoning problems. However, the benefits and limitations of grounded reasoning are understudied. We study where and why grounded reasoning is most useful. To do so, we introduce a chain-of-thought analysis method to measure how much a...

title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
abstract: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a...

title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
abstract: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. Our autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's...

title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
abstract: Modern video models possess strong visual priors, yet do not natively represent human action in metric 3D space. We present EgoGeneralist, which adapts pretrained video generators to unify action-conditioned egocentric video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation. Our role-adaptive action renderer provides video-native representations for multidirectional action-video...

title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
abstract: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware. This migration is (1) a practical need, since it unlocks different hardware for researchers, and (2) a natural...

title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
abstract: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions. We ask when such a quantity is identifiable from an experiment's access, continuous in the mechanism...

title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
abstract: To interpret a direction in a language model's residual stream, we can look for text that strongly activates it. But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains. We develop Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs), language models which map residual stream directions from a subject model to text exemplars that strongly activate those directions....

title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
abstract: Adversarial Training (AT) is an important method for improving model robustness. We study the dynamics of deterministic Gradient Descent (GD) in AT. Most existing works in this direction focus on the small or vanishing step sizes regime, where GD resembles a continuous-time flow. However, such step sizes can make training inefficient and are rarely used in practice. In this paper, we study the AT...

title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning? We systematically compare vanilla reverse-KL OPD with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) across task difficulty, student and teacher size, domain, and...

title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
abstract: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. We ask whether preserving recovered procedures and decisions improves subsequent...

title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
abstract: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a...

title: A Hidden Markov Preference Model for Online Prediction of Adversary Actions
abstract: A defender anticipating an attacker needs a probability distribution over the attacker's next action from information available before that action occurs. Two structures complicate this: the attacker's behavioral regime persists and can switch within an episode, and each action combines an operation with state-dependent arguments whose feasible values change over time. We capture both with a...

title: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception
abstract: Cyclist fatality rates remain high despite policy support for active travel, and autonomous vehicles add complexity to mixed traffic. Neither crash statistics nor multi-model detection pipelines scale to continuous monitoring of perceived safety along a route. We present an edge-assisted crowdsensing system: handlebar cameras supply street-level frames, a vision-language model (VLM) turns each...

title: Label-Wording Augmentation in a Typed-Decision Encoder: Gains on Unfamiliar Words, Not on Abbreviations or Codes
abstract: Typed-decision models score options that the caller supplies at request time, so their accuracy depends on label wording that the model's developer does not control. We compare two releases of a 307M-parameter multilingual cross-encoder, Ru-Jev, trained on thirteen Russian-language tasks; the later release adds an augmentation that presents labels in several surface forms. Holding questions fixed...

title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
abstract: Neural networks are likely to be among the most consequential artefacts in human history. As these systems become more capable and autonomous, their potential to cause societal harm also grows, making AI safety one of the defining challenges of our time. Yet we continue to build increasingly powerful systems without fully understanding how they work, how they will behave in unfamiliar situations,...

title: SM4RT: Cascaded Feed-forward Model for 4D Reconstruction
abstract: We introduce SM4RT, a multi-task cascade feed-forward model for dynamic scene reconstruction from RGB videos. While existing feed-forward approaches typically address geometry reconstruction and motion estimation separately--and often predict motions in a single coordinate frame that must account for camera movement--SM4RT solves these tasks sequentially by first reconstructing 3D geometry and...

title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
abstract: LLM-based medical assistants that follow a patient across visits need a memory that keeps the patient's clinical state correct as it changes. We examine the errors of five memory systems on longitudinal medical dialogue and find three recurring causes: the retrieved evidence gives an outdated state, includes another person's health facts, or lacks a safety fact the answer depends on. We present...

title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
abstract: Chat remains the default surface for many large language model (LLM) tasks, even as agentic tools such as OpenCode excel at coding and automation. Yet the model sees the current dialogue but not the workspace around it. We explore meta access---giving the assistant a structured, permissioned view of the interface itself and propose a ladder of levels: feature tutoring; metadata, settings, and...

title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods...

title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
abstract: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are...

title: On the limitations of molecular representations
abstract: Molecular representations such as fingerprints and learned embeddings play a central role in cheminformatics and small-molecule machine learning. They serve as the primary input for a diverse array of tasks, including clustering, dataset splitting, and virtual screening, yet their evaluation is often limited to downstream model performance on narrow benchmark tasks. title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
abstract: Coding agents are among the most economically consequential deployments of LLMs to date, making reliable evaluation increasingly important. Yet even benchmarks that are carefully validated at release can become stale. As models improve, they can discover valid solutions that existing verifiers reject, while changes to evaluation infrastructure can invalidate assumptions embedded in tasks and...

title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is commonly used in both supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), often under similar optimizer settings. Yet, how the different dynamics of the two stages manifest in the low-rank increment that LoRA optimizes remains unclear. Tracking the singular spectrum and subspaces of LoRA updates on mathematical reasoning tasks, we find that RL concentrates...

title: T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable end-to-end robot control, but inference is increasingly expensive. Each decision processes hundreds of visual tokens, often across multiple cameras, leading to substantial computation while allowing irrelevant background content to distract action prediction under distribution shift. We argue that these issues stem from two complementary forms of...

title: The Gold Rush in AI4Math, II: What are signatures of AI-assisted Proofs?
abstract: The growing use of AI in mathematics raises a question: can we detect AI involvement in proofs, separately from AI assistance with writing? Historical arXiv papers, recent papers disclosing substantive AI use, and manuscripts released by OpenAI provide a rich empirical basis for studying this question. However, several challenges remain: lack of matched case-control pairs; potential...

title: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs
abstract: Uncertainty quantification is crucial in scientific machine learning, where models inform safety-critical tasks such as flood forecasting, financial risk management, and thermal control in machines. title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
abstract: Humanoid robots are typically trained as solitary agents, leaving them unable to coordinate physically with human partners who naturally anticipate and adjust to one another. To bridge this gap, we present Social Humanoid, a hierarchical system that generates and executes socially responsive whole-body motion on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 conditioned on a human partner's motion. title: StepBack: Step-Level Error-Localized Resampling for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning
abstract: Self-consistency (SC) is a widely used decoding strategy for improving chain-of-thought reasoning, but it requires sampling many complete reasoning trajectories with a preset budget. Its efficient variants reduce the cost mainly by stopping full-trajectory sampling early or distributing the number of samples across questions. In this paper, we propose StepBack, a step-level error-localized...

title: Synthesis of Ovarian Cancer Multi-Omics Datasets: A Biology-Informed Evaluation Framework
abstract: Paired multi-omic cancer cohorts are costly to assemble and difficult to share, motivating synthetic cohorts as a complementary resource. As generative model development accelerates, we shift the focus from proposing yet another architecture to defining evaluation criteria that determine whether synthetic data preserve biologically relevant structure. title: Adaptive Low-Light Enhancement for Road Anomaly Detection: A Multi-Architecture Benchmark and Edge Deployment Study
abstract: Road anomaly detection systems on autonomous vehicles must function reliably under degraded visual conditions including darkness, rain, and Harmattan dust haze. title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
abstract: Designing healthcare strategies requires anticipating their clinical and operational consequences before implementation, a task that often relies on health system simulation. Such a simulation necessitates modeling how patient states evolve and generate care demands. title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Imbalanced Landing-Phase Safety Event Prediction from Flight Data
abstract: Landing-phase safety-event prediction requires the detection of rare abnormal approaches within strongly imbalanced multivariate flight data. Capturing coupled temporal behavior while distinguishing event-specific signatures across airport operating contexts remains a central modeling challenge. title: FedReason: Large Language Models as Weight-Space Meta-Aggregators for Heterogeneous Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning servers combine client models with a fixed aggregation rule, and each rule in common use is designed for one kind of heterogeneity. We study whether a large language model (LLM) that inspects the client models can choose the rule itself, without any training on the server. In FedReason, the LLM is called every ten rounds. title: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Different optimizers impose different geometries on parameter updates. Adaptive methods such as Adam and AdamW use coordinate-wise updates, while matrix-aware optimizers such as Muon utilize weight-matrix structure through orthogonalized updates. title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
abstract: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. Gated delta-rule models decay this state and erase its prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value; Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) generalizes this with channel-wise decay and decoupled, full-rank erase and write gates. title: MOMASPLAT: Dynamic Novel-View Demonstration Augmentation for Mobile Manipulation
abstract: Visuomotor policies trained through imitation learning are highly sensitive to changes in camera viewpoint. This is particularly problematic for mobile manipulation (MoMa), where robots rarely execute manipulation from the exact same base pose used during demonstration collection due to navigation uncertainty, localization drift, and environmental constraints. title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
abstract: Current medical benchmarks typically break down clinical competence into isolated factual questions, single-image tasks, or static case vignettes. These tests score individual answers, but reveal less about whether a model can integrate subspecialty knowledge with multimodal evidence and track a patient's condition throughout a course of care. title: VisionSIM: Beyond Idealized Sensors - A Multi-Modal Simulator for Robot Perception
abstract: Robotic perception increasingly relies on heterogeneous sensor suites combining cameras with emerging modalities (event, SPAD, iToF/dToF, and thermal). title: SHORE: Stability-Hybrid On-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Online Bin Packing
abstract: Online 3D bin packing with a processing buffer requires choosing which box to pack, its orientation, and its placement while keeping the stack stable under unknown future arrivals. A collapse ends the episode and forfeits the remaining volume. title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference
abstract: Quantization reduces the memory and bandwidth demands of large language model (LLM) inference but can degrade accuracy; offloading higher-precision data can instead stall generation. title: OraRefer: Segmentation-Guided Multi-Photograph Fusion for Oral Cancer Screening with Guaranteed Patient-Level Sensitivity
abstract: Oral cancer and the oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD) that can precede it are visible on the oral mucosa, which makes smartphone photographs a promising tool for screening. title: A Theoretical Analysis of a Bilevel Optimization Formulation for Combined Local-Global Optical Flow Models
abstract: This paper analyzes a bilevel formulation for learning the regularization parameter of combined local-global (CLG) optical flow models. The lower-level problem computes the flow from a Lucas--Kanade data term and a quadratic or total variation (TV) regularizer, and the upper-level problem selects the parameter that minimizes the squared distance to a ground-truth flow. title: Unifying Central Flow, Rod Flow, and the Edge Coupling
abstract: At the edge of stability, the iterates of gradient descent oscillate along the sharp directions of the Hessian. This poses a significant challenge for continuous-time models as the usual continuous-time approximation -- the gradient flow -- admits no oscillations. title: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching
abstract: Background and Objective: Our main goal is ultrasound guidance: moving a probe until its image matches a target view. Published methods for each part of a guide are evaluated in separate simulators. We asked whether these methods, combined into one guide, are good enough. abstract: Millimeter-wave radar resolves the micrometer displacements of a moving body as micro-Doppler, enabling gait, gesture, activity, pose and vital-sign sensing. title: Enhancing Local and Global Structure in Compressed AI Agent Memory
abstract: AI agents store text as embedding vectors and compress them at scale. A compression is accepted when each item's nearest neighbors survive, but agents also consolidate, delete, and compare memories, tasks that depend on which items lie far apart. abstract: In general-sum games, self-interested learners can reach outcomes that are poor for everyone, which has motivated methods that shape the opponent's learning. title: InstantHand: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Animatable Hand Avatar Reconstruction from a Single Image
abstract: Hand avatar reconstruction typically relies on multi-view capture or per-subject optimization, limiting its scalability. We introduce InstantHand, a feed-forward framework that constructs an animatable 3D Gaussian hand avatar from a single image using off-the-shelf MANO, camera, and mask estimates, without test-time optimization. abstract: Stroke represents one of the leading causes of long-term motor dysfunction on a global scale. title: Spyglass is a framework for reproducible and shareable neuroscience research.
abstract: Scientific progress depends on reliable and reproducible results. Progress can be accelerated when data are shared and re-analyzed to address new questions. abstract: Recent advances in fMRI-based semantic decoding and visual reconstruction have achieved remarkable progress. However, severe inter-subject variability and the scarcity of paired fMRI-image data remain major obstacles to cross-subject generalization. abstract: This study reviews fabrication strategies and performance optimization for flexible brain-computer interface electrodes, covering materials selection, structural design, and signal fidelity improvements.

abstract: Inspired by dragonfly wings, authors propose a vein-membrane hybrid structure strategy and develop a freestanding submicron electrocorticography electrode array.

abstract: Presents an innovative intracortical brain-computer interface to bridge the gap between laboratory settings and real-world navigation for people with paralysis.

abstract: Brain-computer interfaces are moving from task-specific neural decoders toward AI-mediated systems. This work examines how AI assistance layers can lead to neuroadaptive overfitting and proposes slow-fast training strategies.

title: Towards neuromorphic neurotechnologies: integrating brain-inspired computing with brain-computer interfaces
abstract: Explores integration of neuromorphic computing principles with brain-computer interfaces to create more efficient, adaptive neurotechnologies.

abstract: Brain–computer interfaces have achieved transformative success in restoring movement and communication. However, extending these approaches to decoding or recovery of cognitive function poses fundamentally new challenges.

title: Shared latent representations of speech production for cross-patient speech decoding
abstract: Current speech brain-computer interfaces rely on patient-specific decoding approaches. Here, the authors show that patient-specific data can be aligned to a shared space that preserves speech information, enabling cross-patient speech BCIs.

title: Sensory-guided human-machine joint learning accelerates the acquisition of motor imagery brain computer interface control
abstract: Motor imagery brain-computer interfaces are promising neurotechnologies but limited by slow user learning and unstable decoder adaptation. Here, the authors develop a novel sensory-guided joint learning framework that coordinates subject learning and decoder adaptation to improve BCI acquisition.

abstract: Introduces self-supervised consistency enhanced disentangled learning to improve neural decoding generalization across sessions and subjects in brain-machine interfaces.

abstract: Proposes a unified framework for sensory restoration via brain-computer interfaces, covering efferent and afferent pathways and outlining a convergence roadmap for clinical translation.

abstract: Explores how 6G communication technologies could enable next-generation brain-computer interfaces with massive multi-user support, bidirectional real-time neural interfaces, and semantic neural signal interpretation.

title: Mapping Brain-Computer Interface Research in Depression (1995-2026): A Bibliometric Analysis.
abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have emerged as promising tools for neuromodulation and emotion regulation in depression. This study aimed to systematically map the global research landscape, thematic evolution, and emerging trends of BCI applications in depressive disorders through bibliometric analysis.

title: Neural processing of natural speech by adults with and without dyslexia: Evidence for atypical temporal sampling of speech information in the delta and theta EEG bands.
journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
abstract: Neural oscillations in the delta (.5-4 Hz) and theta (4-8 Hz) bands play a key role in tracking the temporal structure of speech. According to Temporal Sampling (TS) theory, dyslexia arises from atypical oscillatory sampling of the speech signal in these bands during infancy and childhood, which is particularly disruptive regarding phonological encoding. abstract: Graph-theoretic analysis provides a rigorous mathematical framework for investigating molecular architecture; however most existing studies primarily rely on conventional topological indices and centrality measures that characterize connectivity without explicitly quantifying structural control, redundancy, vulnerability or resilience. title: Adaptive graph convolutional neural network incorporating ECG for individualized motor imagery EEG classification.
journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
abstract: The recognition of motor imagery electroencephalogram (EEG) signals, which non-invasively capture the macroscopic electrical activity of the brain, is critical for medical rehabilitation and intelligent control. title: Combined effects of an ointment comprising Eisenia fetida oil, Valeriana officinalis, and zinc oxide nanoparticles on healing in a rat model of second-degree burns.
journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
abstract: Burns are one of the most devastating traumatic injuries, and in cases of advanced burns, patients require urgent and specialized care to minimize mortality. Studies have shown that a variety of herbal medicines and nanoparticles can be used to treat burn wounds. title: Event-related potential dynamics of unilateral lower limb movement with functional connectivity analysis.
abstract: Locomotor lateralization represents a general evolutionary trait in primates and is particularly well documented in human upper limb movements. Whether a corresponding lateralization pattern exists in lower limb movements, however, has remained largely unexplored.

title: Urodynamic Voiding Patterns in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: This study aimed to describe urodynamic voiding patterns in patients with MS (PwMS) using standardized assessments, and to compare the performance of the available nomograms and indices for obstruction and bladder contractility.

title: Differences in Urodynamic Findings of Robot-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy Before and 2 Years After Surgery.
abstract: Numerous studies have investigated changes in urinary function following robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP); however, most studies have primarily focused on identifying predictors of postoperative urinary incontinence. This study aimed to evaluate bladder function and lower urinary tract symptoms through urodynamics examined before and 2 years after RARP.

title: Decoding EEG-based cognitive load using fusion of temporal and functional connectivity features.
journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
abstract: Evaluating cognitive load using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals is a crucial research area in the field of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI). title: HEGNet: EEG and EMG fusion decoding method in motor imagery and actual movement.
journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
abstract: The widespread adoption od brain-computer interface (BCI) has been hindered by the limited classification accuracy of electroencephalography (EEG) signals alone.
